maria (runtime): heads up — after running long-context soak (8h, batch mix ~p50 long sequences) I see steady memory growth tied to KV page stitching. flamegraph + heap snapshot attached in thread
cheng: can you paste the repro command? also which branch/commit?
maria (runtime): repro: `./run_perf.sh --model redwood-7b --sequence 16k --duration 8h --mix 90/10` on commit `main@c3d2a1f`. heap diff shows ~120MB growth every 2h on worker-0
ashley: hmm did you try disabling page coalescing/merge? last time that mask exposed an alignment bug
maria (runtime): yes tried `KV_PAGE_MERGE=0` — growth stops, but latency tail increases a bit. suggests merge path is leaking or misaligning offsets
noah: any evidence of cross-request tags in the pages? like previous request ids lingering in metadata
maria (runtime): grep on page headers shows mixed request ids for pages that were stitched: excerpt:

```
page_id=0x7f8a tag=req-12345
page_id=0x7f8a tag=req-67890
```

so the same physical block contains fragments from different requests after merge
cheng: that sounds like a race in the stitch/evict path. maybe a missing fence between page copy and metadata update.
ashley: can you try patching the atomic commit order? swap the updates so we write the metadata before flipping `page->valid = true` and run short repro
maria (runtime): will try. also captured perf samples: kernel selection time spikes at the same points as merge windows. might be a hotspot where merge holds locks and delays eviction leading to reuse of freed slots incorrectly
perf-bot: nightly-perf-tests failed on redwood-7b soak (memory_growth) — job: #4821 — link: https://ci/reports/4821
noah: if merging depends on transient kernel choices we might need to avoid merging under heavy batching. a heuristic: don't merge pages when concurrent_users > 16 or when long_context_mode=true
ashley: agree. temporary mitigation: set `KV_MERGE_THRESHOLD=100` and add stray-tag assertions in debug builds to catch cross-request contamination early
maria (runtime): local patch: swapped metadata/order + added assert in `page_commit()` checking `page->owner == expected_owner` before marking valid. short repro looks stable for 1h. pushing PR now: https://reviews/r/1234
cheng: nice. please include a small unit test that simulates concurrent stitch+evict with randomized ordering. that caught similar earlier bugs
maria (runtime): adding it. will run the 8h soak tomorrow after CI passes. thanks all :thumbsup:
noah: if CI passes can we ship as a canary to dedicated pool? want to monitor memory over 24h before full rollout
maria (runtime): yep — plan is canary -> monitoring dashboard (mem-growth series, page-stitch count, stale-tags) -> gradual rollout
perf-bot: canary deployment scheduled: canary/dedicated/gpu-a -> 2109877000
ashley: also log the page header crc in debug to detect silent corruption (cheap check)
maria (runtime): good call. adding CRC and an emergency kill switch env `KV_FAIL_ON_CRC=1` for canary
noah: great thread. if anyone sees similar in other models ping runtime. i'll follow up with an infra ticket to add a persistent counter for "mixed-owner-stitch" events in the console
